title: Stability Sandbox Protocols for Progressive Rollouts (WIP)
content:
PURPOSE
This is a working doc that captures the experimental ‘stability sandbox’ approach for progressive rollouts. The sandbox is a small, instrumented environment (lightweight synthetic traffic + mirrored production traces) where we run staged exposures before real traffic slices. Aim: detect systemic regressions (latency amplification, tail errors, cache churn) and validate fallback behavior for multi-model routing, KV cache warmup, and autoscaling hooks.

SCOPE
- Applies to features that change inference routing, model variant selection, batching/caching heuristics, and any console-driven traffic slicing logic.
- Not for data-modeling experiments (training-time) or UI-only copy edits.
- Intended as step between internal canary + unit tests and full public A/B.

GOALS / ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1) Detect degradations that manifest under production-like burst profiles (99.9th latency regressions, cache hit-rate drop > 8pp).
2) Confirm fallbacks operate with <= 500ms additional latency and without error amplification.
3) Validate telemetry and alerting thresholds (no false positives > 10% in sandbox) so that production alarms remain meaningful.
4) Produce human-readable test artifacts (replay traces, sample request corpus, timeline of infra events) that can be attached to PRs.

KEY DEFINITIONS (quick)
- Stability Sandbox: ephemeral environment that consumes captured/mirrored traffic plus synthetic stress scenarios.
- Prefix warming window: execution time where we feed cached tokens to regenerate KV hit-rates prior to exposure.
- Escape hatch: pre-defined rollback procedure and traffic switch (automated) if a stability alarm fires.

SANDBOX ARCHITECTURE (notes)
- Lightweight cluster (2-4 gpus) isolated from Dedicated pools. Mirror proxy copies ~2% of production reads (non-PII) and replays them.
- Synthetic burster that can replay tail-heavy sequences at configurable QPS and sequence length distribution.
- Observability hooks: per-request trace id mapping (sandbox-), per-model cost breakdown, cache hit/miss, batch sizes, GPU utilization, oom/retry rates.
- Canary-to-sandbox handoff: PR annotates the sandbox run id for traceability.

RUN TYPES (examples)
- Warmup run: 15–30m feed of historical traffic window + prefix warming. Goal: reach steady KV cache hit-rate.
- Spike stress: 5–10m high-QPS burst with 95/99 latency targets observed.
- Cold start sweep: multiple node restarts with traffic ramp to validate autoscaler behavior.
- Regression replay: targeted request corpus that previously triggered issues (e.g., batch misalignment bug).

METRICS TO WATCH (primary)
- p50/p90/p99 generation latency per model variant (ms)
- Token-per-second throughput and average batch size
- KV cache hit-rate (global and model-specific)
- GPU mem pressure and OOM/retry counts
- Error rates: client-400s, model-runtime-5xx, fallback-invocations
- Observability quality: fraction of requests with full traces attached

ALERT / ESCALATION HEURISTIC (quick sketch)
- Tier 1 (auto-fail): p99 latency > baseline + 35% for 3 consecutive minutes OR error-rate spike > 4x baseline sustained for 2m => auto-fallback to previous routing and mark sandbox run failed.
- Tier 2 (ops review): KV hit-rate drop > 8pp and tail latency degrade 15-30% => notify oncall + owning PD.
- Tier 3 (info): small transient spikes (< 2x baseline) => record for PR notes, no action.

COMMUNICATION & DECISION FLOW
1) Engineer opens PR and chooses ‘run sandbox’ checkbox in CI. PR must attach: run profile, dataset id, expected safe-profile thresholds.
2) Sandbox run executes; results posted to PR as link (artifact bundle: traces, trace-summary, infra timeline).
3) If auto-fail triggers, PR blocked and incident ticket auto-created (PROD-1345-like template).
4) If Tier 2, ping #platform-rollouts + oncall via webhook with brief run summary and link.
5) Owner must respond within 1 hour; decision: continue, reconfigure, or abort rollout.

SIMULATION MATRIX (what to run vs why)
- Model variant swap (A->A-q4 + fallback path): warmup + spike. Why: ensure quantized variant does not amplify latency due to smaller batch nuclei.
- Routing rule change (heuristic by latency/cost): cold start sweep. Why: verify fallback routing is honored under node churn.
- Batching threshold change (max_batch_size): warmup + regression replay. Why: check that effective batch-size distribution remains within hardware limits.
- KV cache TTL change: long warmup (1h) then spike. Why: validate cache churn under realistic session reuse.

CHECKLIST (run owner before sandbox run)
- [ ] Test dataset annotated and scrubbed (no PII)
- [ ] Expected thresholds documented in PR description
- [ ] Observability dashboard link included
- [ ] Rollback playbook referenced and auto-switch enabled
- [ ] Notified impacted stakeholders in calendar (SRE, PD, DS)

EXAMPLE FAILURE SCENARIOS & RESPONSES
- Scenario: p99 doubles during spike, but error-rate stays low. Response: trigger graceful fallback to prior routing variant, keep traffic mirrored for debugging; collect sample traces; escalate to eng owning model.
- Scenario: KV hit-rate collapses after deployment, causing repeated OOMs. Response: drain traffic, scale down new nodes, restore previous cache snapshot, open incident ticket.

OPEN QUESTIONS / DECISIONS NEEDED
- How long should a sandbox run be considered authoritative? (current proposal 1h but some features may need 4h warmup)
- Do we allow non-engineer stakeholders to trigger sandbox runs from Console? (pros: faster; cons: unsafe)
- What synthetic traffic templates should be standard (chatty vs long-tail) — maintain a curated library?
- How to capture cost metrics in a sandbox so they reflect production unit economics without incurring full spend?

NEXT STEPS (short)
- (Ethan) prototype an automated run-step in CI that posts artifacts to PR (due: 2026-01-05).
- (Lucia) draft run templates for three traffic shapes: chatty, bursty, long-tail (due: 2026-01-20).
- (Maya) design the simple ‘escape hatch’ API (action: switch-to-previous-routing) and implement a basic rollback webhook (due: 2026-02-02).

REFERENCES / LINKS
- Confluence rollout safety cookbook: confluence:rollout-safety-cookbook-7
- Example PR with sandbox run: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/pull/98
- Related Jira: PROD-1345 (sandbox incident template)

NOTES TO SELF (informal)
- Keep the UX simple: checkbox + small dropdown of run profiles. Too many knobs has previously blocked adoption.
- Sandbox should be cheap to run — aim for < $50 per 1-hour run in infra spend to encourage use in PRs.
- If we get many false positives, iterate on alert rules rather than turning off automatic rollback.

-- end of working notes --

(If you want to run a quick trial, ping me directly in Slack @maya and include PR link and desired profile.)
